Locked-off camera, framing holds. On the first beat all seven chop their outstretched arms down hard and drop into a knee bounce together. On the next, the small woman in the canary-yellow coat, in the middle of the wedge, jabs a finger straight at the lens; the men either side lean toward her, palms rocking side to side. CRIMSON nods deep on every downbeat. MARINE swings his arm up late and points; SILVER shrugs, palms up, then chops again. She moves with swagger and attitude the whole time: chin up, hips leading, a loose bratty shoulder roll on the beat, never stiff. They never stop: a new move every beat, bouncing in their places. Masks, gloves and clothes stay unchanged; dust drifts, the parked cars stay put. SFX: shoes scuffing dry crust, cloth swish, gloved claps, wind. No voices.

Thanks.
